thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 decode latency breach in prod (svc=decode, cluster=us-west-2). p99 up to 4.2s, p95 creeping to 1.1s, streaming stalls reported by multiple customers. Auto-mitigation did NOT trigger. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/prod/decode?p=latency

alex: seeing the same. spike started ~10m ago. correlates with a burst of kernel-level page faults on a subset of GPUs.

maria: quick context — we shipped a build last night that bumps TRT and applies a new compile-time allocator change (allocator_v2) to improve small-allocation perf. runtime-eng did that. could be related.

kai: do we have the deploy details? which commit and which flag toggled?

deploy-bot: Deploy record: commit abc1234 by runtime-eng @2175554200 — bump TRT 8.2.1 + ENABLE_ALLOCATOR_V2=true in runtime image. Canary -> prod. No rollout pauses.

priya: if allocator_v2 increases background memory churn it could cause KV cache evictions and increase decode tail. We should try reverting the allocator flag on a few hosts before full rollback. quick test: patch the deployment replica set env var:

```bash
kubectl set env deploy/decode-runtime ENABLE_ALLOCATOR_V2=false -n prod
# or patch node-level config: /etc/redwood/runtime.conf
```

alex: applied the env toggle to 3 canaries (usw2-a). immediate effect: p99 dropped from 4.2s -> 1.6s on those hosts. p95 unchanged across region yet. logs show fewer major page faults after toggle.

maria: good catch. sounds like allocator change is increasing page-in activity under our expected working set. Could be different alignment/algo causing more kernel faulting.

kai: can we hotfix without full image rollback? looks like the env toggle is effective. we should patch autoscaler/traffic to shift 15% off affected pools while we verify.

priya: proposing mitigation plan:
- immediate: set ENABLE_ALLOCATOR_V2=false via k8s to all runtime replicas in us-west-2 (rollback allocator change)
- short term: revert TRT bump if issues persist after allocator revert
- medium term: add memory-pressure metrics to runtime and add automatic fallback when major-fault-rate > threshold

runtime-eng: ack. executing env patch across region now.

deploy-bot: Patch job started for deploy/decode-runtime -> ENABLE_ALLOCATOR_V2=false (rolling update). job id: patch-2175554321-01

alex: rolling update completed in us-west-2. observed global p99 drop from 4.2s -> 0.9s over ~6m. streaming stalls dropped considerably.

maria: collecting heap/alloc traces from one affected host to send to runtime team for root cause. plucking a few jemalloc stats and syscall traces.

kai: great. any customer-facing impacts to report? we have a handful of errors from streaming sessions timing out.

sre-oncall: opened incident ticket INC-2175554321. Customer success notified for high-touch customers with active sessions. See notes: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2175554321

priya: status update for execs: mitigated via allocator toggle, p99 restored below SLO, continuing postmortem. Next steps: full rollback of TRT bump if traces show allocator is not the only factor.

runtime-eng: we found allocator_v2 introduced a different mmap/munmap pattern that triggers kernel page reclaim under our workload; not purely TRT. We'll prepare a small diff to reintroduce allocation-to-slab batching to avoid churn.

alex: handoff — I will monitor p95/p99 across regions for the next 2 hours and collect all traces. tagging @sre-oncall to take monitoring baton at 22:00 UTC.

sre-oncall: taking handoff. will watch key dashboards and escalate if p99 > 1.5s or major-fault-rate rebounded.

maria: logging for the postmortem: suspect change = runtime image abc1234 (ENABLE_ALLOCATOR_V2=true) + TRT bump; symptom = p99 tail and streaming stalls; root cause = allocator churn causing paging/reclaim pressure; mitigation = env toggle false -> p99 recovered; follow-up = allocator fix or rollback, add guardrails for future allocator/compiler changes.

kai: nice quick mitigation. please attach the kernel traces and jemalloc stats to the incident when available.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. severity = Sev2. timeline updated: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2175554321/timeline

priya: thanks all. we'll schedule a postmortem with runtime and infra next sprint. :thumbsup:

runtime-eng: noted, will prepare a minimal repro and a test in staging that exercises allocator churn under our decode workload.

sre-oncall: closing friction — leaving this thread open for traces and the postmortem link. will update last_message_ts when we close the incident.
